indicators.note: ahead says the piece before it is placed in front of the other piece

parts.note: sound as in healthy and intact, as in 'safe and sound'

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the seaman is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a seaman is a sailor; said out loud it matches the ending needed

explanation.surface: A seafaring merchant tells of a sound heard up ahead of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' says the sound piece goes in front of the seaman piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler is a trader who sells goods in bulk to retailers, a kind of merchant.

parts.note: to sow seeds is to plant them
A is the standard abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener sows a patch of ground among the fruit trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' reads as the female pig, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy tropical banana-like fruit, usually cooked before eating.

indicators.note: the wood comes round, wrapping itself about the other piece

parts.note: bark is the woody outer layer of a tree

indicators.note: turning round makes the short word 'to' face the other way

parts.note: the word to, turned about

explanation.surface: A woodworker gradually warms to a particular composer's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a twentieth-century Hungarian composer, famous for string quartets and folk-based works.

indicators.note: in sequence says to set the chosen pieces one after another

parts.note: four compass points, south, east, west and north, chosen from the available directions

explanation.surface: A sailor tacks, picking each change of course in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacked is from sewing, not sailing, despite the nautical feel of the directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is loose temporary stitching, so tacked fabric has been sewn together.

indicators.note: new suggests these letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged
the printed word is split: its first half is the signal, its second half joins the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sleeping newborn baby is utterly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newborn' looks like one word, but the anagram signal is hiding as its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone personable is pleasant in manner and looks, and so attractive or likeable to others.

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so its letters need setting another way

parts.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: The figure for the capital city on a pie chart has been miscalculated.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital is the architectural sense, not a city or money.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapiter is an old architectural term for the head or top part of a column, its capital.

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
the clue appeared in the Guardian, so the paper's things are 'our' things

explanation.surface: A strange story appearing in the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the newspaper that printed this puzzle, so it speaks of itself as 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour is unverified talk passed from person to person, a hearsay report.

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
T is the abbreviation for time
the printed word is read as its two halves

explanation.surface: A cosy chat over afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teatime' must be split into its two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal friendly talk between people.

clue.text: Glimmer of understanding of semivowel sound

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the phrase is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a semivowel taken literally is half of a vowel, and I is one of the vowels

explanation.surface: A linguistics student begins to grasp what a semivowel sounds like.
explanation.walkthrough: Semivowel is a real phonetic term for sounds like W and Y, which disguises the jokey literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Having half an eye on something means giving it only slight attention, a faint inkling.

indicators.note: whoever drinks takes something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: Hugh is a man's name, any fellow
no as nothing, the round letter like zero

explanation.surface: A teetotal man refuses the German white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock looks like the wine; it is the joint in an animal's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Hough is a Scottish word for the hock, the joint in the hind leg of a horse or cow, or meat from it.

parts.note: long describes something tall and thin in shape

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the word not flips end to end

parts.note: taken as written, then turned over
the printed word is split into the turning signal and the definition

explanation.surface: A tall, thin person insists they are not overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overweight' must be split: 'over' turns the word before it and 'weight' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A long ton is the imperial unit of 2,240 pounds, a measure of weight used in Britain.

clue.text: Second game in court to be slotted in

indicators.note: slotting in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sport is a game
up as in 'up before the magistrate', appearing in court

explanation.surface: A second match is to be fitted into the tennis court schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Second is the verb, as in seconding a motion, not a unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it, giving it formal support.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a loud kiss on the lips or cheek

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the gesture of blowing a kiss, but blow and kiss are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sharp hit with the open hand and a noisy, hearty kiss.

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving without sense, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Hospital doctors unwisely ask nurses out on dates.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctors is a verb, not the medical staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to tamper with it, and denaturing changes a substance's nature, often to make it unfit to drink.

clue.text: Deny turning, through time, into corrupt being

indicators.note: going through something means running inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: turning makes the word for deny face the opposite way

parts.note: to renege is to go back on or deny a promise

explanation.surface: Constant denials over time turn someone into a corrupt person.
explanation.walkthrough: The deny word sits between the D and the ATE of the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A degenerate is a person who has fallen to low moral standards, a depraved individual.

clue.text: Quality of King and Queen recognised in very many quarters

indicators.note: to be recognised in somewhere is to be found inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a string of compass points: south, east, east, north, east, north, east, south, south
R stands for both Rex (king) and Regina (queen)

explanation.surface: The royal couple are well known in many parts of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: A single R serves for both monarchs, since Rex and Regina share their initial; quarters are the points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sereneness is the state of being calm and untroubled, a quality of character.

parts.note: surface reading: a stammer or lisp that hinders someone's talking; setter's reading: anything that blocks communication between speakers of different tongues

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the medical sense is the bluff.
explanation.definitionFit: When two people share no tongue, the gap between them stops their talk, literally impeding speech.

clue.text: Claims to have originally raised standards

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so this piece is put at the front

parts.note: something raised is up
rights are things one is entitled to claim

explanation.surface: Campaigners say they were the first to push for higher standards.
explanation.walkthrough: Standards are posts or upright supports, not levels of quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprights are vertical posts, and a standard can mean an upright pole or support.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pictures in the mind, supposes
second meaning: plural of imago, the adult winged stage of an insect

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that butterflies are just one example of the insects meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pictures in the mind, and as a noun it is the Latin plural of imago, a fully developed adult insect.

clue.text: Restore order — that's the bottom line

parts.note: the rear is the bottom or backside
a range is a line or row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A manager tidies things up and declares that this is final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bottom line' looks like a phrase meaning the upshot, but it splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange things is to put them into a new arrangement, perhaps tidying them back into order.

clue.text: Too protective of one new girl

indicators.note: to be protective of something is to shelter it, wrapping round it

parts.note: too in the sense of also, as well
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is overly protective of a single new girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a common female first name, as needed for a girl.

clue.text: Flat found in high-rise on returning home

indicators.note: a high-rise points upwards, so the high thing is read going up, from its end
returning means going back, so the piece is read the other way

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: An apartment located in a tower block, reached on coming back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, matching the high-rise, but means level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is a broad area of flat, level land.

indicators.note: something grasping holds on tight, so it closes around the other piece

parts.note: pushy means forcefully self-assertive
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A wealthy, pushy person greedily courting a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Plushy means luxurious and opulent, like plush fabric, so rich in appearance.

clue.text: Clothes drier — horse under another name, say

indicators.note: say asks for the word to be spoken, keeping its sound but not its spelling

parts.note: a ringer is a horse raced under a false identity in place of another

explanation.surface: A laundry gadget and a horse racing under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: A wringer is the old-fashioned mangle that squeezes water out of washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wringer presses water out of wet laundry, so it is an appliance that dries clothes.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the River ... in north-east England, flowing through Durham
second meaning: to sport clothes is to have them on

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a water sport, but sport is a verb meaning to have on, as with a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a river through Durham and also means to have clothing on the body.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an extremely funny person, 'a real scream'
second meaning: an official reprimand or alert

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like shouting out an alert; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, an amusing or outrageous person is 'a caution', and the word also means a word of warning.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a harvest of grain or vegetables
second meaning: the handle or stock of a whip, especially a riding whip

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like farm goods kept in store, but the second sense is a part of a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest of plants is a crop, and the word also names the stock of a whip or the short riding whip itself.

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the round letter, to be removed
the printed word is read as its two halves

explanation.surface: Someone takes on the role of a fusspot who ignores nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fusspot' must be split into its two halves, and the O removed from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a manner or attitude is to take it on, to assume it.

clue.text: She lost to possible champ? Such couldn't!

indicators.note: possible hints at one of several outcomes, so the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: the letters of these three words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is beaten by someone who may become a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Champ here is the verb, to chew noisily; the whole clue also describes why a creature without teeth could not do so.
explanation.definitionFit: Champing means chewing hard, which a creature lacking teeth could not manage.
